summary: Issei Suzuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sophia University and completed a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.

István Tamaskó was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna and under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen, later becoming a professor at the Evangelical Lutheran Lyceum in 1838.

Italo Pizzi was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Pisa, he held posts at the Laurentian Library, University of Florence, University of Naples Federico II, and University of Turin.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguistics and Japanology scholar who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She has served as a teaching professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University and the University of Kharkiv, he held posts at the Kunstkamera, Saint Petersburg State University, and the Institute of Linguistics.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, Buddhologist, and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1858 to 1862 and served on the university's Faculty of Oriental Studies from circa 1869 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber, Vasily Vasiliev, and Kaetan Kossovich, later becoming a privatdozent and professor at Saint Petersburg State University.
Ivan Stchoukine was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Pelliot and Alfred Foucher.

Ivanna Otroshchenko is a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian, and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. She earned her degree at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv and joined the A. Yu. Krymskyi Institute of Oriental Studies in 1998.

Ivar Ulrik Wallenius was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the Royal Academy of Turku. He served as Docent of Arabic at the Royal Academy of Turku and Associate Professor of Oriental Literature at the University of Helsinki.

Ives Goddard was a linguistics scholar who was educated at Harvard College and Harvard University. He later held posts at Harvard University, the Smithsonian Institution, and the National Museum of Natural History.
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.
Ivo Fišer was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Friš. He held positions at Charles University and the University of Copenhagen.

Iwao Ishikawa is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. He has held appointments at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nichiki Kimura and earned a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan.
Iwao Shima was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Nagoya University and served as a professor at Kanazawa University.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. She has served as an assistant professor and director at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a Japanology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She has served as a teaching professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).
